questions.question: Which Indian Mass Movement began with the famous ‘Dandi March’ of Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Civil Disobedience Movement**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement** was initiated by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930.
 
• The movement began with the famous **Dandi March**, where Gandhi and his followers marched to the Arabian Sea to produce salt from seawater, defying the British salt tax.
 
• This movement was a pivotal part of the Indian independence struggle and aimed at resisting British rule through nonviolent means.
 
• The Dandi March covered a distance of approximately 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, Gujarat.
 
• The movement saw widespread participation from various sections of Indian society, including women, students, and peasants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Non-Cooperation Movement** was launched by Gandhi in 1920 but was called off in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.
 
• The **Quit India Movement** was started in 1942, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• The **Kheda Movement** was a peasant struggle in 1918 led by Gandhi in the Kheda district of Gujarat.
 
• The **Dandi March** and the subsequent Civil Disobedience Movement marked a significant escalation in the Indian struggle for independence.

questions.question: The length of the men's kabaddi court is _____ metres.

• The game is also featured in various international multi-sport events, including the Asian Games.
 
• Kabaddi is known for its unique blend of physical strength, strategy, and agility, making it an exciting and dynamic sport to watch and play.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Directive Principle based on the ideals of Mahatma Gandhi?

options.text: To promote industrialisation in urban areas
To prohibit intoxicating drinks and drugs that are injurious to health
To promote cottage industries in rural areas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To promote industrialisation in urban areas**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **To promote industrialisation in urban areas** is **NOT a Directive Principle based on the ideals of Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government, and they aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi's ideals focused on rural development, self-sufficiency, and prohibition of intoxicants.
 
• Examples of Gandhian principles in the Directive Principles include **organising village Panchayats**, **prohibiting intoxicating drinks and drugs that are injurious to health**, and **promoting cottage industries in rural areas**.
 
• These principles reflect Gandhi's vision of a self-reliant and sustainable rural India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are enshrined in **Part IV **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They are** not enforceable by any court**, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The principles aim to promote the welfare of the people by securing a social order in which justice, social, economic, and political, shall inform all the institutions of national life.
 
• They are inspired by the Directive Principles given in the Constitution of Ireland and also reflect the ideals of the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• While they are non-justiciable, these principles act as a beacon for the State to achieve the goal of a welfare state.

questions.question: Which of the following methods is used to calculate national income by summing up the total incomes earned by individuals and businesses in an economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Income method**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Income method** is used to **calculate national income by summing up the total incomes earned by individuals and businesses** in an economy.
 
• This method considers the incomes earned by various factors of production, including wages, rents, interests, and profits.
 
• It provides a comprehensive view of the income distribution within the economy.
 
• The Income method helps in understanding the economic performance and the contribution of different sectors to the national income.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other methods to calculate national income include the **Value-added method**, the **Output method**, and the **Expenditure method**.
 
• The **Value-added method** calculates national income by adding the value added at each stage of production.
 
• The **Output method** calculates national income by measuring the total output produced within the economy.
 
• The **Expenditure method** calculates national income by summing up total expenditures made in the economy.
 
• Each method provides a different perspective on the economic activities and helps in cross-verification of the national income estimates.

questions.question: What is personal income?

options.text: The income earned by individuals and households after taxes and other deductions
The total income earned by businesses and corporations in an economy
The income earned by individuals through their own business or self-employment
The total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Personal income** is the total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions.
 
• It includes wages, salaries, bonuses, social security benefits, dividends, interest, and rental income.
 
• Personal income is a measure of the **financial resources available to individuals and households for spending and saving**.
 
• It is an important economic indicator used to assess the economic well-being of the population and to predict future consumer spending.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disposable income** is the **income available to individuals and households after taxes and other deductions**.
 
• It represents the amount of money that can be spent or saved according to personal preferences.
 
• Personal income and disposable income are key metrics in macroeconomic analysis and policy-making.
 
• Understanding the levels and trends of personal income helps in assessing the overall economic health and planning for fiscal policies.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Who founded the Hindu reform organisation Brahmo Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** founded the Hindu reform organization **Brahmo Samaj** in **1828**.
 
• Brahmo Samaj was established with the aim of** reforming and modernizing Hindu society**.
 
• The organization played a significant role in the social and religious reform movements in India during the 19th century.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is often referred to as the "**Father of Modern India**" for his efforts in promoting education, women's rights, and the abolition of practices such as sati.
 
• Brahmo Samaj emphasized the worship of one God and discarded rituals and idol worship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** was born on May 22, 1772, in Radhanagar, Bengal.
 
• He was a key figure in the Bengal Renaissance and worked towards the eradication of social evils in India.
 
• He also campaigned against the **caste system and child marriage**, and for the rights of women, including the right to inherit property.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy's efforts led to the abolition of the practice of sati by Lord William Bentinck, the then Governor-General of India, in 1829.
 
• He also **founded the Atmiya Sabha**, which later became part of the Brahmo Samaj movement.

questions.question: ___________ word of Indian dance is derived from a Sanskrit word and literally means ‘taking towards’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abhinaya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abhinaya** is derived from the Sanskrit word and literally means '**taking towards**'.
 
• It is an important aspect of Indian classical dance and involves the art of expression.
 
• Abhinaya encompasses the dramatic and expressive aspects of the dance, focusing on conveying emotions and storytelling.
 
• It is one of the four main components of Indian dance, the others being** Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (expressive dance), and Natya (dramatic dance)**.
 
• Abhinaya is crucial in making the performance more engaging and connecting with the audience on an emotional level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indian classical dance has a rich history and is deeply rooted in the cultural and spiritual traditions of India.
 
• There are several classical dance forms in India, including Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Kathakali, each with its own unique style and technique.
 
• The Natya Shastra, an ancient Indian treatise on performing arts, is considered the foundational text for Indian classical dance and theatre.
 
• Abhinaya is detailed extensively in the Natya Shastra, outlining the various types of expressions (**Angika, Vachika, Aharya, and Sattvika**) used in performances.
 
• Mastery of Abhinaya requires rigorous training and practice, as it involves nuanced facial expressions, gestures, and body movements to effectively convey the intended emotions and narrative.

questions.question: What are the three tiers of the Government in India?

options.text: Union government, Judiciary government and Federal government
Union government, State Government and Federal Government
Union government, State government and Judiciary government
Union Government, State Government and Local Government

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Government, State Government and Local Government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The three tiers of the Government in India** are the **Union Government, State Government, and Local Government**.
 
• The Union Government is also known as the Central Government and has the authority to govern the entire country.
 
• The State Government governs individual states within the country.
 
• The Local Government operates at the grassroots level, including municipalities and panchayats.
 
• This three-tier system helps in decentralizing the power and administration, ensuring better governance and more effective public service delivery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** establishes this three-tier system to ensure a balance of power and responsibilities between different levels of government.
 
• The **Union List**, **State List**, and **Concurrent List** in the **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution specify the subjects on which each tier of government can legislate.
 
• The Union Government deals with matters of national importance, the State Government handles regional issues, and the Local Government focuses on local administration and community needs.

questions.question: The foundation of Sanchi Stupa was laid by which of the following Kings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashoka**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashoka**, the great Mauryan emperor, laid the foundation of the **Sanchi Stupa**.
 
• The Sanchi Stupa is one of the oldest stone structures in India and an important monument of Indian architecture.
 
• It was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• The Stupa is located in Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh, and is a **UNESCO World Heritage site**.
 
• The structure was built to house the relics of the Buddha and serves as a significant site for Buddhist pilgrimage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka** ruled the Maurya Dynasty from 268 to 232 BCE and is remembered for his role in spreading Buddhism across Asia.
 
• He embraced **Buddhism after the Kalinga War**, which prompted him to adopt a policy of non-violence and spiritual conquest.
 
• The Sanchi Stupa is an example of Ashoka's efforts to promote Buddhism and his patronage of Buddhist architecture.
 
• Inscriptions and carvings on the Sanchi Stupa provide valuable insights into the art, culture, and religious practices of ancient India.
 
• Ashoka's edicts, inscribed on pillars and rocks across the Indian subcontinent, emphasize moral and ethical conduct, non-violence, and religious tolerance.

questions.question: During which months do retreating monsoons occur in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**October and November**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **October and November** are the months during which **retreating monsoons** occur in India.
 
• The retreating monsoon, also known as the** northeast monsoon**, marks the period when the southwest monsoon winds start to retreat from the Indian subcontinent.
 
• This season is characterized by the withdrawal of monsoon clouds and a decrease in rainfall in most parts of the country, except for the southeastern coast.
 
• During this time, Tamil Nadu and parts of Andhra Pradesh receive significant rainfall due to the northeast monsoon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **southwest monsoon** typically arrives in India in **early June and lasts until September**, bringing heavy rainfall and accounting for most of the annual precipitation.
 
• The **northeast monsoon** is less intense compared to the southwest monsoon and primarily affects the southeastern coast of India.
 
• The retreat of the monsoon is a gradual process, and the transition period can lead to a mix of weather patterns, including occasional thunderstorms and cyclones.
 
• Understanding the monsoon patterns is crucial for agriculture, water resource management, and disaster preparedness in India.

questions.question: Which is the primary structural component responsible for most of the mechanical strength of the cell wall?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cellulose**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cellulose** is the primary structural component responsible for most of the mechanical strength of the cell wall.
 
• It is a complex carbohydrate or polysaccharide consisting of a linear chain of several hundred to many thousands of **β(1→4) linked D-glucose units**.
 
• Cellulose is the most abundant organic polymer on Earth, making up about 33% of all plant matter.
 
• It provides tensile strength to the cell wall, enabling it to withstand turgor pressure and maintain the shape of the cell.
 
• In addition to providing structural support, cellulose also plays a crucial role in plant growth and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heparin** is an **anticoagulant**, not involved in cell wall structure.
 
• **Glycogen** is a form of energy storage in animals and fungi, not a structural component of the cell wall.
 
• **Chitin** is a structural component in the cell walls of fungi and the exoskeletons of arthropods, but not in plants.
 
• Cellulose is synthesized by cellulose synthase enzymes located on the cell membrane.
 
• In industrial applications, cellulose is used in the production of paper, textiles, and various chemical products.

questions.question: Which of the following oceans is surrounded by the continent of North America and South America to the east?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atlantic Ocean**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atlantic Ocean** is the ocean that is surrounded by the continent of North America and South America to the east.
 
• The Atlantic Ocean is the second-largest of the world's oceans, covering approximately 20% of Earth's surface.
 
• It separates the "Old World" from the "New World" and has been a critical route for exploration, trade, and travel.
 
• It connects to the Arctic Ocean in the north and the Southern Ocean in the south.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Pacific Ocean** is located to the west of North and South America and is the largest ocean on Earth.
 
• The **Indian Ocean** lies to the east of Africa and south of Asia, bordered by the Arabian Peninsula and Australia.
 
• The **Arctic Ocean** is the smallest and shallowest of the world's five major oceans and is located around the Arctic Circle.
 
• Oceans play a crucial role in regulating the Earth's climate and are home to diverse marine ecosystems.
